    Home/Switch broadband — we coordinate eligible OTS switches

    Switch broadband — we coordinate eligible OTS switches

    For eligible residential broadband and landline switches, One Touch Switch lets the gaining provider coordinate the provider-to-provider steps. Here is how OCCTA handles the order-specific process.

    The short answer

    Where One Touch Switch applies, the gaining provider coordinates the switch. Your expected activation or switch date, engineer requirement and any known downtime risk are confirmed for the actual order.

    On this page

    1. 01How One Touch Switch works
    2. 02What we cover
    3. 03Keeping your number
    4. 04Timeline
    01

    How One Touch Switch works

    You order with us. Where One Touch Switch applies, the providers coordinate the switch and you receive the required switching information, including any charge from your existing provider. The expected date and any known downtime risk are confirmed for the order; we do not promise zero downtime.
    02

    What we cover

    Any current OCCTA switching promotion or credit is shown explicitly in the order or written quote before acceptance. We do not promise reimbursement of another provider’s early-termination charge unless that specific promotion is offered and recorded for your order.
    03

    Keeping your number

    Add Digital Home Phone at signup and we'll port your landline number as part of the switch — no separate porting form.
    04

    Timeline

    Day 0 order, Day 1–2 notification, Day 10–14 switchover. FTTP-to-FTTP moves can be same-week; new-build FTTP installs need an engineer slot (2–4 weeks).

    Want us to sanity-check your switch?

    Postcode + your current provider — we'll tell you what to expect and any likely fees, before you commit.

    We only use your details to help with your enquiry. See our privacy policy.
